answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents partition the network into a trusted core lagoon and quarantine clusters onto an unverified island. During each consensus pulse, random multi-agent auditor committees perform topological cut verifications across bridge nodes. If cross-cluster auditing exposes fabricated identities, correlated stake slashing instantly penalizes the conspirators. Because bridging cuts across colluding subgraphs requires quadratic bond deposits, Sybil creation imposes a superlinear attacker cost.
